1.stem_plain: My teammates and _________ gifted the new student a new soccer ball to commemorate the start of _________ new soccer journey in our school.

2.stem_plain: The student _________ the teacher spoke about is also an excellent chef.

3.stem_plain: "The librarian arranged the books neatly, _________ she?" asked Mrs Lam.

4.stem_plain: If it _________, you would have gotten wet.

5.stem_plain: Neither the twins nor Alona _________ Dev's stories.

6.stem_plain: The Lim Bo Seng Memorial was annouced as a national monument _________ memory of one of Singapore's war heroes.

7.stem_plain: Not until they had discussed the topic _________ they _________ on their project.

8.stem_plain: _________ how hot and dry the weather is, you must still exercise.

9.stem_plain: _________ that the accused was innocent, some members of public decided to show support for him despite the backlash.

10.stem_plain: The tourist from Myanmar spoke _________ English and it was difficult to speak to her.

1.concept: 物主代词 — Compound subject + possessive
1.zh: 队友和我送给新生一个新足球，纪念他在我校开始新的足球旅程。
1.note: 并列主语用主格 I；his 指代 the new student 的所有格；陈述句一般过去时 gifted。

2.zh: 老师谈到的那名学生也是出色的厨师。
2.note: 关系代词 whom 指人作宾语；陈述句一般现在时 is。

3.concept: 反意疑问句 — Question tag — past simple
3.zh: “图书管理员把书排得整整齐齐，不是吗？”林太太问。
3.note: 附加问句 (Question tag)：一般过去时 arranged，用 didn't she；间接引语。

4.concept: 虚拟语气 — Third conditional — If it had rained
4.zh: 要是当时下雨了，你就会淋湿。
4.note: 第三条件句 (Third conditional)：与过去事实相反，从句 had + 过去分词。

5.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject–verb — neither … nor
5.zh: 双胞胎和阿洛娜都不喜欢德夫讲的故事。
5.note: neither … nor 就近一致，Alona 为单数，动词 enjoys；陈述句一般现在时。

6.concept: 介词 — Preposition — in memory of
6.zh: 林谋盛纪念堂被宣布为国家古迹，以纪念新加坡一位战争英雄。
6.note: 固定搭配 in memory of；被动语态 was announced；一般过去时。

7.zh: 直到讨论完这个话题，他们才开始做项目。
7.note: Not until 倒装：did + 主语 + 动词原形 work；时间从句用过去完成时 had discussed。

8.zh: 不管天气多么炎热干燥，你仍必须锻炼。
8.note: regardless of 表“不管”；祈使句 must still exercise。

9.zh: 相信被告无罪，一些公众仍决定支持他，尽管会遭到强烈反对。
9.note: 现在分词短语 Believing 表原因；主句一般过去时 decided。

10.zh: 那位来自缅甸的游客几乎不会说英语，很难和她交谈。
10.note: little + 不可数名词 English；陈述句一般过去时 spoke。

11.stem_plain: The firefighter's reassurances were not effective in _________ the little girl's concerns about her pet dog in the burning building.

12.stem_plain: The man was imprisoned after making _________ remarks and hurting the sentiments of a minority group.

13.stem_plain: Kelly, the head prefect, _________ confidence when she delivered her farewell speech to the graduating cohort.

14.stem_plain: The long-distance runner realised that he was way ahead of his competitors and decided to _________ for a bit before his final burst.

15.stem_plain: "Just because you have _________ in rank does not mean you can treat your subordinates badly," Maxine said to her boss.

11.zh: 消防员的安慰未能有效减轻小女孩对宠物狗在着火大楼里的担忧。
11.note: 选（1）allaying：allay concerns 固定搭配“缓解担忧”；陈述句一般过去时。
11.concept: 词汇辨析 — allaying（减轻；缓解）

choices.zh: 减轻，缓解；消除（动词的现在分词，指通过解释、安慰或提供证据，去消除、减少或平息内心的恐惧、担忧、怀疑或痛苦等负面情绪）
choices.eg: The firefighter's calm reassurances were unfortunately not effective in allaying the little girl's intense concerns about her pet dog trapped inside the burning building.

choices.zh: 完成，结束；润饰（动词的现在分词，指将某项工作、比赛、任务或学业带入到最后的收尾阶段并彻底做完，或者对物品表面进行最后的抛光美化）
choices.eg: The construction crew is currently finishing the final safety inspections on the newly built pedestrian bridge before it opens to the public next week.

choices.zh: 停止，阻拦；中断（动词的现在分词，指使正在移动、发生、运转的人、车辆、活动或机械完全停下来，或者指制止某种不良行为的延续）
choices.eg: The abrupt stopping of the train inside the dark tunnel caused a wave of mild panic among the passengers before the conductor made an announcement.

choices.zh: 扑灭，熄灭；毁灭（动词的现在分词，指利用水、化学灭火剂或沙子使燃烧的火苗、火灾或香烟彻底熄灭，亦可引申指破灭某人的希望或热情）
choices.eg: The emergency response team spent hours extinguishing the volatile chemical fire that had threatened to blow up the entire industrial park infrastructure.

12.zh: 那人因发表贬损言论伤害少数群体感情而被监禁。
12.note: 选（2）derogatory：侮辱性言论；被动 was imprisoned。
12.concept: 词汇辨析 — derogatory（贬损的；侮辱性的）

choices.zh: 变形的，畸形的；损毁的（形容词，指物体的本来形状、外观或结构由于受到外力挤压、疾病、火灾或先天缺陷而发生严重改变，变得不规则或丑陋）
choices.eg: The metal frame of the bicycle became completely deformed after it was crushed beneath the heavy wheels of the delivery truck.

choices.zh: 贬损的，侮辱性的；有失体面的（形容词，指言论、态度或文字带有强烈的轻蔑、不尊重或批判色彩，旨在故意损害他人的名誉、尊严或形象）
choices.eg: The man was sentenced to imprisonment after making derogatory remarks online that deeply hurt the religious sentiments of a minority group.

choices.zh: 使人衰弱的，使人无力的（形容词，指某种严重的疾病、长期慢性的身体疼痛或极为恶劣的经济环境，不断消耗并彻底削弱一个人的体能、精力或意志力）
choices.eg: The elderly patient found it incredibly difficult to walk independently after battling a debilitating muscular disease for over five years.

choices.zh: 令人灰心的，使人沮丧的（形容词，指某个糟糕的消息、失败的结果或残酷的现实极其令人失望，从而彻底消磨掉一个人的斗志、信心或积极性）
choices.eg: It was truly disheartening for the young athletes to see their months of rigorous physical training canceled along with the tournament.

13.zh: 级长凯莉在向毕业年级致告别辞时充满自信。
13.note: 选（1）exuded：exude confidence 流露自信；时间从句 when + 一般过去时。
13.concept: 词汇辨析 — exuded（散发；流露）

choices.zh: 散发，流露；渗出（动词，指一个人自然而然地暴露出某种强烈的特质、情感或态度，让人清晰地感受到，亦指皮肤、植物分泌或渗出液体、气味）
choices.eg: Kelly, the head prefect, exuded absolute confidence and poise when she delivered her inspiring farewell speech to the graduating cohort.

choices.zh: 发出，放射；排放（动词，专门指某种光源、热源、机器或烟囱，向空气中释放出光线、热量、刺耳的噪音、气体、辐射或有毒烟雾）
choices.eg: The specialized laboratory equipment constantly emitted a low, rhythmic humming sound while processing the biological samples.

choices.zh: 随后发生，接着发生；结果是（动词，指由于某一个突发事件、误会或激烈的争吵作为导火索，紧接着随之而来发生了一系列连锁反应或必然结果）
choices.eg: When the referee made a highly controversial decision, a massive argument ensued between the rival players and their head coaches.

choices.zh: 逐渐发展，演变；进化（动词，指某种语言、技术、商业模式、传统或生物，在漫长的时间流逝中，经过一步步的微调逐渐变得更加复杂、成熟或先进）
choices.eg: The small family-owned grocery shop successfully evolved into a multi-national online retail empire over the course of three decades.

14.zh: 长跑选手发现自己遥遥领先，决定在最后一冲前稍微放慢一点。
14.note: 选（4）let up：暂时放缓节奏；decided to + 动词原形。
14.concept: 词汇辨析 — let up（放松；减缓）

choices.zh: 使失望，辜负；放下，放长（动词短语，指未能达到他人的期望、未能履行承诺而使人感到沮丧，或者指放长衣服、降下旗帜）
choices.eg: The young athlete promised his dedicated coach that he would train harder and would not let down his supporters in the upcoming finals.

choices.zh: 放开，松手；解雇，释放（动词短语，指停止用手紧握某物或某人，或者指由于公司缩减开支而解雇员工，亦引申指放弃执念或过去的记忆）
choices.eg: You must let go of the safety handle only when the roller coaster ride has come to a complete and proper standstill inside the station.

choices.zh: 泄露（秘密），吐露；假装（动词短语，常用于否定句或疑问句，指在说话时不经意地透露出保密的信息、意图或隐藏的事实）
choices.eg: Although Ken already knew about the grand surprise birthday party his friends were planning, he did not let on and acted completely clueless.

choices.zh: 放松，减缓；停止，停歇（动词短语，指某种糟糕的天气、剧烈的疼痛或紧张的工作状态在强度上有所减弱，亦指人在努力奋斗中放慢脚步）
choices.eg: The long-distance runner realised that he was way ahead of his competitors and decided to let up for a bit before saving his energy for the final burst.

15.zh: “你资历高并不意味着可以恶劣对待下属，”玛克欣对老板说。
15.note: 选（1）seniority：in rank 指职级资历；间接引语。
15.concept: 词汇辨析 — seniority（资历；年资）

choices.zh: 资历，年资；级别高（名词，指因在某公司或机构工作时间更长，或在军衔、职位上更高而享有的优先权或崇高地位）
choices.eg: “Just because you have seniority in rank does not mean you can treat your subordinates badly,” Maxine said boldly to her boss.

choices.zh: 权威，权力；官方机构（名词，指组织或法律赋予某人的管辖权、发号施令的合法权力，亦指政府管理部门或行业专家）
choices.eg: The school discipline master has the absolute authority to suspend any student who repeatedly violates the code of conduct.

choices.zh: 下等，劣势；自卑感（名词，指在质量、价值、技能或地位上低于他人，亦经常专门用于形容心理上的自惭形秽）
choices.eg: The psychologist explained that constant criticism from parents can easily instill a deep sense of psychological inferiority in young children.

choices.zh: 优越性，优势；优越感（名词，指在质量、技术、数量或阶层上明显高于、好于他人，亦可指因自视甚高而表现出的傲慢态度）
choices.eg: The defending champions demonstrated their tactical superiority on the field by dominating the football match from start to finish.

16.concept: 近义词 — heinous（非法的；不正当的）
16.note: 形容词 heinous 意为极恶劣的、可鄙的。在此网络行为考查语境下，用于形容越界且违法的恶意举动，与 illicit（非法的，不正当的，违禁的）互为考卷上的近义替换选项。

choices.zh: 非法的，不正当的，违禁的
choices.eg: The cybercrime division was set up to crack down on any illicit activities on social media.

choices.zh: 引出，诱出，启发（动词）
choices.eg: The English teacher designed interactive tasks to elicit a lively response from the pupils.

choices.zh: 征求，请求，招揽（意见/捐款等）
choices.eg: The local charity group went door-to-door to solicit donations for the historic flooded estate.

choices.zh: 明确的，清晰的，直白的
choices.eg: The laboratory supervisor provided explicit instructions to ensure the safety of all technicians.

17.concept: 近义词 — pass off as（假装是）
17.note: 动词短语 pass off as 意为冒充、假装成。在描写网络虚假身份的命题语境中，它直接对应高频动词短语 pretend to be（假装是，装作）。

choices.zh: 揭示为，显现出是（常见结构为 reveal it to be）
choices.eg: Thorough background checks completed by the tech firm revealed him to be a professional fraudster.

choices.zh: 相信是，认为（常见结构为 believe it to be）
choices.eg: Based on the security certificates provided, local engineers believe the server to be perfectly safe.

choices.zh: 假装是，冒充，装作
choices.eg: These online trolls often pretend to be innocent users before spreading malicious rumors.

choices.zh: 确认是，查明是（常见结构为 ascertain it to be）
choices.eg: Independent inspectors arrived early to analyze the factory data and ascertain it to be correct.

18.note: 形容词 contentious 意为容易引发争论的、有异议的。在讨论网络话题或社会焦点时，直接对应同义词 controversial（有争议的）。

choices.zh: 暴力的，猛烈的
choices.eg: The sudden dispute near the gate unfortunately escalated into a violent clash between the two groups.

choices.zh: 激烈的，强烈的，慷慨激昂的
choices.eg: The newly appointed council members engaged in a vehement debate over the annual dynamic budget.

choices.zh: 有争议的，引发争论的
choices.eg: The manager decided to postpone the presentation to avoid bringing up a controversial topic.

choices.zh: 对抗性的，挑衅的
choices.eg: The assistant was reminded that using a confrontational tone during the interview was inappropriate.

19.note: 副词 purportedly 意为声称地、据称、据说。在表示缺乏真实证据但主观宣称的学术辨析中，直接对标常用副词 supposedly（据称，据说，应当）。

choices.zh: 公认地，无可否认地，诚然
choices.eg: Admittedly, completing the 100km super marathon in a single day was an exceptionally hard task.

choices.zh: 反复地，一再地
choices.eg: The primary school pupils were warned repeatedly not to leave their bags in the open canteen.

choices.zh: 据说，据称，应当
choices.eg: Some misguided individuals defend these trolls, supposedly acting in the name of free speech.

choices.zh: 无疑地，必定
choices.eg: Through months of relentless practice, he is undoubtedly the best candidate for the title.

20.note: 动词 meander 本意指河流蜿蜒或人在街头漫步、闲逛，在网络空间的文学比喻描写中，引申为无特定目的地浏览，对应核心词汇 roam（漫游，闲逛）。

choices.zh: 潜伏，埋伏（网络用语指“潜水”）
choices.eg: Anonymous internet trolls love to lurk online, waiting for an opportunity to launch attacks.

choices.zh: 走，步行
choices.eg: The local residents enjoy taking a quiet walk along the scenic river path every evening.

choices.zh: 漫游，闲逛，流浪
choices.eg: When you roam the vast expanses of the Internet, remember to treat others with kindness.

choices.zh: （野兽等）潜行觅食，暗中巡游
choices.eg: The wild tiger spent hours on the prowl through the thick jungle, searching for its next meal.

cloze: How does one deal with online trolls? These trolls with their [Q16 (heinous)] schemes have made it difficult for many online users to enjoy the Internet. They [Q17 (pass off as)] innocent online users at first. When the time is right, these users often leave behind vile comments on [Q18 (contentious)] online topics that provoke other users into an argument. Despite being disturbed by the rise of such trolls, many other users have come to defend them, [Q19 (purportedly)] under the banner of free speech. There is no real solution to trolls unfortunately. As you [Q20 (meander)] the vast network of the Internet, the best you can do is practise graciousness and kindness.
zh: 如何应对网络喷子？这些喷子用极其恶劣的伎俩让许多网民难以安心上网。他们起初假装成无辜用户，时机一到就在易引发争论的话题下留下恶毒评论，挑起争吵。尽管许多人对喷子泛滥感到不安，仍有人以言论自由为名为他们辩护。遗憾的是没有真正解决办法；漫游互联网时，最好以礼貌与善良待人。

21.stem_plain: What is the main purpose of the event?

options.1: to show people the wonders of nature
options.2: to share interesting facts about edible plants
options.3: to get students to volunteer as ambassadors
options.4: to encourage people to start their own edible gardens

22.stem_plain: The Miniature Garden workshop teaches participants to _________ .

options.4: monitor how their vegetables are growing

23.stem_plain: In the section 'How to make a Seed Ball', which of the following statements is true?

options.1: A seed ball contains only one seed.
options.2: Birds and animals enjoy eating the seed balls.
options.3: The craft paper provides nutrients for the seeds to grow.
options.4: A mixture of compost and clay is used to wrap the seeds.

24.stem_plain: Mila wants to take the guided tour around the farm. She _________ .

options.1: should make payment at the booth
options.2: should register for the tour at 3 p.m.
options.3: will be able to taste some of the fruits
options.4: will get to try out new farming methods

25.stem_plain: According to the excerpt from Nature Magazine, what is one concern that Singaporeans have when it comes to urban farming?

options.3: The amount of pesticide farmers use
options.4: Supermarkets only have produce from other countries

26.stem_plain: According to the excerpt, City Farm builds 'edible gardens'. What does the term 'edible gardens' refer to?

options.1: gardens that are free of pesticides
options.2: gardens that owners look after themselves
options.3: gardens that produce vegetables and fruits
options.4: gardens that are built in urban spaces like shopping malls

27.stem_plain: City Farm contributes to local farming efforts by _________ .

options.1: offering farm tours and workshops on weekdays
options.2: assisting people with the design of their edible gardens
options.3: going to schools to help students build vegetable gardens
options.4: educating Singaporeans on the need for imported produce

28.stem_plain: What does City Farm look for in a student ambassador?

options.4: The ability to train other students

21.concept: 主旨 — Main purpose — City Farm event（主要目的）
21.note:
Flyer promotes City Farm workshops/tours on starting edible gardens at home → main purpose (4) encourage people to start their own edible gardens.

Other options describe side activities or ambassador recruitment, not the core event aim.

22.concept: 细节 — Detail check — Miniature Garden workshop（信息定位）
22.note:
Workshop theme: grow herbs/vegetables in small containers → (2) grow herbs and vegetables.

Recycling boxes, cooking, or monitoring growth are not the stated focus.

23.concept: 细节 — Detail check — Seed Ball steps（信息定位）
23.note:
Seed-ball instructions: wrap seeds in compost and clay mixture → (4) mixture of compost and clay is used to wrap the seeds.

Single seed, animals eating them, or craft paper as nutrients are not supported.

24.concept: 细节 — Detail check — guided farm tour（信息定位）
24.note:
Guided tour advert mentions tasting farm produce/fruits → Mila (3) will be able to taste some of the fruits.

Payment booth, 3 p.m. registration, or trying new methods are other options.

25.concept: 细节 — Detail check — Nature Magazine excerpt（信息定位）
25.note:
Excerpt cites concern about pesticide use in urban farming → (3) the amount of pesticide farmers use.

Land space, location, or imported produce are distractors.

26.concept: 题型 — Vocabulary in context — edible gardens（题型考点）
26.note:
City Farm builds gardens that grow food you can eat → (3) gardens that produce vegetables and fruits.

Pesticide-free, self-maintained, or mall location are not the definition given.

27.concept: 细节 — Detail check — City Farm services（信息定位）
27.note:
City Farm helps design home edible gardens for residents → (2) assisting people with the design of their edible gardens.

Weekday tours, school builds, or import education differ from the text.

28.concept: 细节 — Detail check — student ambassador（信息定位）
28.note:
Ambassador criteria emphasise passion for gardening/plants → (1) a love for gardening.

Other traits (communication, grades, etc.) are not the keyed requirement.

cloze: The aardvark gets its name from a South African word meaning 'earth pig'. [Q29] the aardvark looks like a pig, especially with its body and snout, aardvarks actually share common ancestors [Q30] elephants and golden moles. Aardvarks are found throughout much of sub-Saharan Africa.

Aardvarks use [Q31] large front claws to dig holes at a rate of 0.5 metres in 15 seconds. This enables them to get to their favourite meal [Q32] termites and ants. Aardvarks have long, sticky tongues with [Q33] they slurp up and swallow tens of thousands of insects from termite mounds and ants nests.

Aardvarks are most active [Q34] night and tend to live alone. During the day, they sleep curled up [Q35] their burrows. As night falls, aardvarks will emerge cautiously from their dens, [Q36] the lookout for predators. They are able to see at night, [Q37] otherwise have poor vision and are colour-blind.

Humans are the aardvark's biggest threat. Some landowners do not like the holes left behind by the aardvarks. The use of pesticides to grow crops on land inhabited by aardvarks [Q38] also reduced the number of insects available for aardvarks to eat. It is not surprising then, that its numbers are decreasing.
zh: 土豚之名来自南非语，意为“地猪”。尽管土豚外形像猪，尤其身体和吻部，其实与大象、金毛鼹有共同祖先。土豚广泛分布于撒哈拉以南非洲大部分地区。
土豚用它们的大前爪挖洞，十五秒可挖半米，以便吃到最爱的白蚁和蚂蚁。它们有长而黏的舌头，可吸进并吞下数以万计的昆虫。
土豚多在夜间活动，常独居。白天蜷缩在洞穴睡觉。夜幕降临时，它们小心出洞，警惕捕食者。它们能在夜间视物，但总体视力差且色盲。
人类是土豚最大威胁。一些地主不喜欢土豚留下的洞。在土豚栖息地上使用农药也减少了它们可食的昆虫，因此土豚数量正在下降。

29.note: although the aardvark looks like a = 结合句意选 although。

31.note: Aardvarks use their large front claws to dig = 结合句意选 their。

32.note: get to their favourite meal of termites and ants. = 看前后搭配，选 of。

33.note: have long, sticky tongues with which they slurp up and swallow = 定语/名词性从句 → which。

34.note: Aardvarks are most active at night and tend to live = 看前后搭配，选 at。

35.note: day, they sleep curled up in their burrows. = 看前后搭配，选 in。

Some time ago, I [Q41(enlist)] Flanagan in a programme to assist children [Q42(which)] have difficulty reading aloud. Most of the children in the programme [Q43(pesieve)] reading as something to be dreaded, but reading to a dog that is not [Q44(jargemantal)] changes everything for them.

During our library time, I unroll Flanagan's paw-print rug in the children's reading corner. Flanagan sits [Q45(ajascent)] to a bright yellow bookcase neatly stacked [Q46(on)] all types of inviting books for a child to read and explore. [Q47(Purched)] on top of the bookcase is an adorable plush puppy with a striking [Q48(rezembalance)] to Flanagan.

zh: 它叫弗拉纳根，是我的四条腿朋友。出生时只有八公斤，血统来自西班牙猎犬家族。它有耷拉的耳朵，尾巴摇个不停，皮毛是棕色的。
不久前，我让弗拉纳根参加一个帮助朗读有困难儿童的计划。大多数孩子原先把阅读视为可怕的事，但对一只不会评判的狗朗读，一切都改变了。
图书馆时间里，我在儿童阅读角铺开弗拉纳根的爪印地毯。弗拉纳根坐在明亮的黄色书架旁，书架上整齐堆满各种吸引孩子的图书。书架顶上放着一只可爱的毛绒小狗，与弗拉纳根惊人地相似。
第一个孩子到来时，弗拉纳根摇尾欢迎，朗读便开始了。弗拉纳根专心听孩子读，有时把爪子放在孩子膝上。每个孩子朗读时那份专注令人赞叹。弗拉纳根听过各种故事；每周它都在改变孩子的人生故事，一个字一个字地。

[Q51] near the Daohugou village in Northeastern China, the perfectly preserved specimen is a close relative of the modern-day spider known as the Golden Silk Orb-Weaver. It is a type of spider known for the impressive [Q52] it weaves.

Experts [Q53] that the fossil is about 165 million years old. What surprises them is its rather large size, which [Q54] about five centimeters when stretched from end to [Q55]. That is because this specimen of spider [Q56] during a period when oxygen levels were much higher, causing similar insects to [Q57] to almost monstrous sizes. For example, back [Q58], dragonflies sported a wingspan of up to a metre, while millipedes measured over two metres.
Similar [Q59] today's Golden Silk Orb-Weaver, this spider also had silk spinning organs on its leg, suggesting that it too was capable of spinning large webs, to [Q60] its prey.

Scientists believe that the ancient spider has been around for over 350 million years [Q61] the Earth was one big supercontinent known as Pangaea. However, the species was well spread out by the time Pangaea [Q62] up into seven continents and can therefore be found in many [Q63] of the world today. Since its close relative thrives in tropical climate, scientists speculate that the Daohugoa region used to be warmer and more humid [Q64] it is today.
Generally, [Q65] are not well-represented in the fossil records as their soft external skeletons do not preserve well. As such, this is a significant find in the world of paleontology.
zh: 科学家在中国东北大沟沟村附近发掘出据信是迄今最大的蜘蛛化石。保存完好的标本是现代金蛛的近亲，以所织的壮观大网著称。
专家称化石约一亿六千五百万年。令人惊讶的是体型：拉直约五厘米。该蜘蛛生活在氧气更高的时期，类似昆虫可长到近乎巨大；例如当时蜻蜓翼展可达一米，千足虫超过两米。
与今日金蛛相似，这种蜘蛛腿上也具吐丝器官，说明也能织大网诱捕猎物。
科学家认为这种古老蜘蛛已存在三亿五千万年以上，当时地球还是名为盘古大陆的超级大陆。盘古分裂成七大洲时该物种已广泛分布，故今日世界多地可见。因其近亲喜热带气候，推测大沟沟村一带曾更暖更湿。
一般而言，蛛形纲动物因外骨骼软而不易形成化石，故此次发现对古生物学意义重大。

51.concept: 过去分词短语充当伴随/地点状语
51.note: 修饰主句主语 the perfectly preserved specimen。指这个标本是在中国东北的道虎沟村附近被“发现”、“出土”或“定位”的，故填过去分词形式 Discovered / Unearthed / Found / Located。位于句首需大写。

52.concept: 名词语意与动词特定搭配
52.note: 作为定语从句 it weaves 的核心宾语。在关于蜘蛛的科学场景下，结合动词 weave（织），与之完美搭配的必然是复数名词 webs，意为它能织出令人惊叹的“蛛网”。

53.note: 主语为复数名词 Experts（专家），本句陈述目前达成的科学共识，用一般现在时。指专家们“估计”、“算出”或“认为”这块化石有1.65亿年历史，故填动词原形 estimate / calculate / state / say / believe。

54.concept: 主谓一致与一般现在时动词
54.note: 关系代词 which 引导定语从句修饰单数名词短语 its rather large size，从句谓语动词需用单三形式。结合后文“从头到尾约五厘米”的数值，指其尺寸“达到（reaches/measures）”或“是（is）”五厘米，故填 measures / reaches / is。

55.note: 与其前置的介词短语 from end to 完美结合。构成英语中用于形容物体首尾总跨度、总长度的经典专属习惯短语 from end to end，意为“从一端到另一端”。

56.note: 主语为这一特定的蜘蛛标本，后接 during a period（在那样的一个历史时期），叙述远古历史，谓语动词需采用一般过去时。指这种蜘蛛“生活”、“存在”或“繁衍”在那个含氧量极高的时代，故填 lived / existed / thrived。

57.concept: 使役结构后的动词原形
57.note: 与前面的使役动词结构 causing similar insects to 完美组合，后接动词原形。指当时的高含氧量促使类似的昆虫“生长（grow）”或“发育成（develop）”近乎怪兽般的庞大体型。

58.note: 与前置词 back 完美结合。构成在各类科学考古、历史讲述中极其核心和高频的专属回溯时间习语 back then，意为“在那个时候/在远古时期”，蜻蜓的翼展能达到一米。

59.concept: 形容词与介词固定搭配
59.note: 后接名词短语 today's Golden Silk Orb-Weaver。完美契合高频常考的经典形容词加介词专属固定句式 be Similar to...，意为与现在的金丝蛛“相似”。

60.note: 不定式符号 to 后接动词原形。在探讨捕食者结网的生物学场景下，指它结出巨网的目的是为了去“捕捉”、“引诱”或“套住”它的猎物，故填入动词原形 trap / catch / capture / snare / lure。

61.note: 引导限定性定语从句，修饰表示时间跨度的先行词 350 million years。当时地球还是一块连成一体的超大古陆，在从句中充当时间状语，故填入关系副词 when。

62.concept: 一般过去时短语动词搭配
62.note: 主语为超级古大陆 Pangaea，后接副词短语 up into seven continents，叙述地质历史。完美契合形容大陆板块分裂、裂开的特定短语动词 split up 或者是 broke up，需用过去时形式。

63.note: 前面有数量形容词 many 修饰，后接介词短语 of the world today。指随着大陆漂移，这种生物如今已经广泛分布并被发现在世界上的许多“地区”、“角落”或“地方”，故填复数名词 regions / parts / corners / places / areas。

64.note: 前文出现了明确的比较级形容词 warmer and more humid。与之呼应并构成跨越时空对比的必然是比较连词 than，用以推测该地区在远古时期比“现在（than it is today）”更加温暖潮湿。

65.concept: 名词语意与文体分类呼应
65.note: 修饰名词主语，后接复数谓语动词 are not well-represented。结合全篇的大主旨，此类生物因为软质外骨骼不易保存而极难形成化石。此处填入代指此类昆虫或蛛形纲的复数名词 spiders / insects / arachnids 均在科学层面上完全正确且符合考卷标准。位于句首需大写。
